messages.author: d561f118e7e9fc17
messages.subject: "INlA.exe has encountered a problem and needs to close" error on previously successful code
parts:
Hello,
I have been running the same code for a few months. However, today when I ran my code, I get an error message:
"Inla.exe has encountered a problem and needs to close".

I have run several of the codes for the examples, and they run. Why would my code no longer run? Has the programming language been changed?

Here is my code:

formula12=habitat2$dens~f(region.struct,model="besag",graph.file="f:/chapter2/inla/habitat.graph",param=c(1,0.05)) +  habitat2$avgtemp+ habitat2$powerb
  result12=inla(formula12,family="zeroinflated.nbinomial.2",data=habitat2,E=rep(1.1,n),control.inla=list(h=0.01),verbose=FALSE,control.predictor=list(compute=T),control.compute=list(dic=1,mlik=1))   # a

parts:
On Tue, 2011-11-22 at 04:07 -0800, Marc Marí-Dell'Olmo wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I have exactly the same problem. Trying to solve: I have upgraded INLA
> [inla.upgrade(testing=TRUE)], I have installed the latest version of
> R, I have outdated INLA [inla.upgrade(testing=FALSE)], I have
> restarted Windows. But none of this has solved the problem. Finally,
> I've solved it by copying an old library INLA folder (C:\Program Files
> \R\R-2.8.0\library\INLA) of another computer and pasting it in my
> computer…
>
>
> Marc

the problem is that one cannot just keep an old version of the R-INLA
library while upgrading R to version 2.14. So either upgrade R-INLA
before upgrading R to version 2.14, or, perhaps safer, remove R-INLA,
then upgrade R, and then reinstall R-INLA from www.r-inla.org

The problem is that R-2.14 require all libraries to have a NAMESPACE
definition/file, and without it, it will refuse to load the library. So
any 'old library' without a NAMESPACE def/file will not be loaded after
the R upgrade.
